````text
# #3842: Patch: the 20-game daily cap holds under simultaneous challenges, seeks and accepts
Opened by @jgoetzmann.

A follow-up to daily games (#3727, merged in #3762), found in its review and left out of it. Part of the tracker #3726.

### What happens

A player may hold at most `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` (20) running games, open seeks and open challenges together (R3727004). [`has_room`](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L82-L88) (`crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs:83`) counts them in one database transaction and commits it; the new challenge, seek or game is written in a later one ([lines 180](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L180), [254](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L254) and [338](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/blob/1964004112/crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs#L338)). Several requests sent at the same moment each see 19, and all succeed, so a player can go past 20.

### What should happen

However many requests arrive at once, a player never holds more than `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES`; the ones past it answer `409 daily_full`.

### How to reproduce

With 19 held, send several challenge (or seek, or accept) requests in parallel. More than one succeeds, and the count goes past 20.

### Fix

Count and insert in the same transaction while holding a per-player lock, for example `select … from public.profiles where id = $1 for update` or `pg_advisory_xact_lock`, in `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`. Keep the in-memory fake (`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`) matching, and add a case to `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` that fails without it (two transactions racing for the twentieth place: one wins, one is refused).

If it needs a migration (a trigger, say), take the next free number after `0089` and register it in `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` (the test prints the checksum to pin) and both lists in `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh`.

Rated hard: concurrency in the store, the Postgres store and the fake kept in step, and possibly a migration.

<!-- jackioh-bot:plan -->
## Plan

_Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43696235891)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

**Goal.** However many challenge, seek or accept requests one account sends at once, it never holds more than `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES` (20) running daily games, open seeks and sent challenges together. Every request past the cap answers `409 daily_full` (R3727004). To get there, the count and the write happen in the same transaction, under a per-account lock, in all four places a write happens: a challenge, an accept, a seek that waits, and a seek that pairs. The Postgres store and the in-memory fake are changed together, and a case in `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` has two transactions race for the twentieth place: one is written and one is refused. No migration is needed, because a transaction-level advisory lock needs no schema.

**Files to touch.**

| Path | new/change | What |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `crates/server/src/db/store.rs` | change | `Tx::daily_lock_account` (dispatch) |
| `crates/server/src/db/pg.rs` | change | `pub async fn daily_lock_account` (advisory xact lock) |
| `crates/server/src/db/fake.rs` | change | `pub fn daily_lock_account` (`call(f, "daily.lock")`) |
| `crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs` | change | module doc, `has_room` doc, new `has_room_locked`, recount in `challenge`, `accept`, `seek`; `reopen_seek` doc |
| `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` | change | `mod daily`: new case `r3727004_two_sends_racing_for_the_last_daily_place_write_one`, import, `both_stores!` entry |
| `crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs` | change | new test `r3727004_a_challenge_an_accept_or_a_seek_whose_rival_took_the_last_place_is_refused` |
| `spec/rulings/R3727004.md` | change | `proven_in` += `crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` |
| `spec/09-architecture.md` | change | §9.13 "Many games at once": "however many arrive at once" |
| `crates/server/README.md` | change | "## Daily games": one sentence on the recount under the lock |

Do not touch: `crates/server/migrations/`, `crates/server/src/db/migrate.rs`, `crates/server/tests/store/migrations_pinned.rs` or `crates/server/tests/sql/run.sh` (there is no migration); `spec/11-rulings.md`, `spec/INDEX.md` or `spec/pending/` (there is no new ruling, since this enforces R3727004 as written); and `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, the engine, cards, AI and web.

The rules that govern this change: §9.13 ("Many games at once"), R3727004, CLAUDE.md rule 9 (the cap stays `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES`) and the server README contract that a store change goes in `tests/store/contract.rs`.

**Steps.**

1. **`crates/server/src/db/store.rs`.** In the second `impl Tx<'_>` (the daily section), right after `daily_active_count` (ends near line 3182) and before `// daily invites`, add:
   ```rust
   /// R3727004, #3842: a lock on the account's daily games, seeks and challenges until the
   /// transaction ends, so two requests at once count and write one after the other (Postgres: a
   /// transaction-level advisory lock; the fake runs one transaction at a time). A lock, no row.
   pub async fn daily_lock_account(&mut self, profile_id: &str) -> StoreResult<()> {
       dispatch!(self, daily_lock_account(profile_id))
   }
   ```

2. **`crates/server/src/db/pg.rs`.** After `daily_active_count` (ends near line 8231) and before `// daily invites`, add this. It copies the pattern of `lock_account` in `crates/server/src/economy/store.rs:2284`:
   ```rust
   /// One lock per account, transaction-scoped like the economy's `lock_account`, under its own key so
   /// a daily send never waits on a pack opening.
   pub async fn daily_lock_account(t: &mut PgTx<'_>, profile_id: &str) -> Result<(), StoreError> {
       run_as(t, Some(profile_id)).await?;
       sqlx::query("select pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('jackioh.daily:' || $1::text, 0))")
           .bind(profile_id)
           .execute(&mut **t)
           .await
           .map_err(db_error)?;
       Ok(())
   }
   ```

3. **`crates/server/src/db/fake.rs`.** After `daily_active_count` (ends near line 5231), add:
   ```rust
   /// Every fake transaction runs alone (it holds the store's one lock until it ends), so it holds the
   /// account's daily lock already; charged to the hooks like every call.
   pub fn daily_lock_account(f: &mut FakeTx<'_>, _profile_id: &str) -> Result<(), StoreError> {
       call(f, "daily.lock")?;
       Ok(())
   }
   ```

4. **`crates/server/src/daily/invites.rs`, imports and helpers.**
   - Line 29: add `Tx` to the `crate::db::store` import.
   - Module doc, lines 14–15: append the sentence "Each is counted again in the transaction that writes it, under the account's daily lock (`Tx::daily_lock_account`), so requests at once never pass the cap (#3842)."
   - Leave the body of `has_room` unchanged. It stays lock-free as the early refusal. Change its doc to: "R3727004: whether `profile_id` may hold one daily game, seek or challenge more, read before the choice is frozen or the game prepared, so a full account is refused cheaply; the write's transaction counts again ([`has_room_locked`])."
   - Directly below `has_room`, add:
   ```rust
   /// R3727004, #3842: the same question in `tx`, the transaction that writes the challenge, seek or
   /// game, under the account's daily lock: requests at once take it in turn, each counting what those
   /// before it wrote.
   async fn has_room_locked(tx: &mut Tx<'_>, profile_id: &str, now: i64) -> Result<bool, ApiError> {
       tx.daily_lock_account(profile_id).await?;
       let held = tx.daily_active_count(profile_id, now).await?;
       Ok(held < i64::from(DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES))
   }
   ```

5. **`challenge`.** In the write transaction (`let mut tx = app.db.begin(Some(&me))` near line 198), between the `are_friends` re-check block and `daily_invites_create`, insert:
   ```rust
   // R3727004, #3842: counted again where the challenge is written, under the account's lock.
   if !has_room_locked(&mut tx, &me, now).await? {
       tx.commit().await?;
       return full();
   }
   ```

6. **`accept`.** In the write transaction (near line 261), insert the same block, with "the game" in the comment, between the `are_friends` re-check and `daily_invites_close`. A refusal there leaves the challenge open, because nothing has been written yet.

7. **`seek`, the own-seek path.** In the transaction near line 381, insert the same block, with "the seek" in the comment, before `daily_invites_create`.

8. **`seek`, the claim path** (lines 346–363). Change the `started` block to answer `Option<String>`:
   ```rust
   let started = async {
       let game = prepare_between(app, &other, match_id, &me, &frozen, now).await?;
       let mut tx = app.db.begin(None).await?;
       // R3727004, #3842: counted again where the game is written, under the account's lock.
       if !has_room_locked(&mut tx, &me, now).await? {
           tx.commit().await?;
           return Ok(None);
       }
       game.create(&mut tx).await?;
       tx.commit().await?;
       game.started();
       Ok::<Option<String>, ApiError>(Some(game.match_id().to_string()))
   }
   .await;
   let match_id = match started {
       Ok(Some(match_id)) => match_id,
       Ok(None) => {
           reopen_seek(app, &other, now).await;
           return full();
       }
       Err(error) => {
           reopen_seek(app, &other, now).await;
           return Err(error);
       }
   };
   ```
   - Update the comment above the block to: "a start that fails, or finds the account full, puts the other's seek back."
   - Update `reopen_seek`'s doc: "A claimed seek whose game failed to start, or whose claimer the recount found full (R3727004), goes back…".
   - Leave the claim transaction itself unchanged: claiming does not move the claimer's count.

9. **`crates/server/README.md`, "## Daily games".** At the end of the paragraph ending "…puts the claimed seek back where it stood." (line 788), append: "R3727004's cap is read once before the choice is frozen, for a quick `daily_full`, and again in the transaction that writes the challenge, the seek or the game, under the account's daily lock (`Tx::daily_lock_account`: a transaction-level advisory lock in Postgres; the fake runs one transaction at a time), so of requests at once only those that fit are written (#3842); a claimed seek whose claimer is full that way goes back too."

10. **`spec/09-architecture.md`, line 285.** Change "and a challenge, a seek or an acceptance past that is refused (`daily_full`)." to "and a challenge, a seek or an acceptance past that is refused (`daily_full`), however many arrive at once."

11. **`spec/rulings/R3727004.md`.** Add `  - crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs` under `proven_in`. This follows R3727008's precedent. Leave the body unchanged.

12. Write the tests below, then run the commands.

**Tests.**

- **`crates/server/tests/store/contract.rs`, `mod daily`.**
  - Add `use jackioh_server::config::DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES;`.
  - After `s913_daily_active_count_counts_running_games_and_open_sends`, add the case `r3727004_two_sends_racing_for_the_last_daily_place_write_one`. Its doc: "R3727004, #3842: two sends racing for an account's twentieth place, each counting under `daily_lock_account` and writing only while the count leaves room. The first has counted and holds its transaction open as the second begins: the second's lock waits for the first's commit, so it counts the first's seek and is refused; without the lock both count nineteen and both write."
  - Body, in this order:
    1. `a`, `b` are `active_profile`; `now = harness.now()`; `cap = i64::from(DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES)`; `let (a_id, b_id) = (a.id.as_str(), b.id.as_str());`.
    2. `for n in 1..cap { daily_game(harness, a_id, b_id, now - 10_000 + n, Some(now + 60_000)).await; }`, then assert `daily_active_count(a_id, now) == cap - 1`.
    3. `let mut first = harness.db.begin(None).await.expect("begin");` then `first.daily_lock_account(a_id)` and `first.daily_active_count(a_id, now)`, asserting the count is `cap - 1`. Map errors with `unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{}: …: {error}", harness.name))`.
    4. `let second = async { begin(None); lock; held = count; let written = held < cap && t.daily_invites_create(&seek(a_id, QueueMode::Random, DAYS, now, now + 60_000), now).await…; t.commit(); written };`
    5. `let rest_of_first = async move { let written = first.daily_invites_create(&seek(a_id, QueueMode::Bo1, DAYS, now, now + 60_000), now).await…; first.commit().await.expect("commit"); written };`
    6. `let (second_written, first_written) = tokio::join!(second, rest_of_first);`
    7. Assert `first_written`, assert `!second_written`, and assert `daily_active_count(a_id, now) == cap`. Every message carries `harness.name`.
  - Add the case name to `mod daily`'s `both_stores!` list (line ~13689).
  - In the fake, the second `begin` waits for the first's commit, so the result is deterministic. In Postgres, the advisory lock makes the second wait.
- **`crates/server/tests/api/daily.rs`.** After the existing `r3727004_…` test (ends line 758), add `#[tokio::test] async fn r3727004_a_challenge_an_accept_or_a_seek_whose_rival_took_the_last_place_is_refused()`.
  - Local `use jackioh_server::db::fake::{CallOutcome, FakeTables}; use jackioh_server::db::store::{DailyInviteKind, DailyInviteRow, DailyInviteState, QueueMode}; use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;`.
  - Loop over `case` in `["challenge", "accept", "seek", "pair"]`, each with a fresh `two_friends()`, plus `cy = person(&app, 3, "Cy")`. Each iteration does the following.
    1. Run `daily_game(&app, &ada, &bo, 14)` `DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES - 1` times.
    2. Set up the case:
       - `"accept"`: Bo POSTs `random_challenge(&ada, 14)`; assert 201 and keep `id`.
       - `"pair"`: Cy POSTs `/api/daily/seeks` `{"mode":"random","perMoveDays":1}`; assert 201.
    3. Build the rival: `rival = DailyInviteRow { id: "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000003842".into(), kind: Seek, from_profile: ada.id.clone(), to_profile: None, mode: QueueMode::Bo1, per_move_days: 7, choice: json!({ "mode": "random" }), state: Open, match_id: None, created_at: 0, expires_at: app.daily.now() + MS_PER_DAY }`.
    4. Install a `before_call` hook, copying the pattern at line 596. It pushes `rival.clone()` into `tables.daily.invites` the first time `method == "daily.lock"` (`once.swap`) and always answers `CallOutcome::Proceed`.
    5. Send Ada's request:
       - `"challenge"`: POST `random_challenge(&bo, 14)`.
       - `"accept"`: POST `/api/daily/challenges/{id}/accept` `{"mode":"random"}`.
       - `"seek"` and `"pair"`: POST `/api/daily/seeks` `{"mode":"random","perMoveDays":1}`.
    6. Clear the hook (`before_call = None`).
    7. Assert `(status, code_of(&body)) == (409, "daily_full")` and that `fired` is true.
    8. Assert Ada's `daily_active_count(ada.id.as_str(), app.daily.now())`, read in its own transaction, `== i64::from(DAILY_MAX_ACTIVE_GAMES)`.
    9. Extra checks per case:
       - `"accept"`: Ada's `GET /api/daily` has `challenges.incoming` of length 1.
       - `"pair"`: Cy's `GET /api/daily` has `seeks` of length 1 and `games == json!([])`.
  - Every message names `{case}`.
  - Without the change, "daily.lock" is never called and the write goes through, so the test fails.
- **Commands:**
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store daily::` (the contract's memory half)
  - `cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server api::daily::` (the existing daily tests stay green, the failed-start reopen at line 957 among them)
  - `sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh` (Docker is available here; this runs the Postgres half). Optionally, for the sanity check that the case fails without the lock: run `KEEP_DB=1 sh crates/server/tests/db/run.sh`, turn `pg::daily_lock_account` into a no-op for one run of `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:postgres@127.0.0.1:55433/jackioh cargo test -p jackioh-server --test server_store r3727004 -- --test-threads=1`, confirm it fails, put it back, and run `docker rm -f jackioh-pg-store-test`.
  - `cargo clippy -p jackioh-server --all-targets -- -D warnings`
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - `cargo jackioh spec check`
  - `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` (no card plays differently, so no fragment is needed)

**Done when.**
- [ ] A challenge, an accept, a waiting seek and a pairing seek each count again under `daily_lock_account` in the transaction that writes them, and answer `409 daily_full` when full.
- [ ] Postgres and the fake both have `daily_lock_account`, dispatched from `Tx`.
- [ ] The new contract case passes in memory and against Postgres (`tests/db/run.sh`).
- [ ] The new API test and every existing `api::daily::` test pass.
- [ ] README, §9.13 and R3727004's `proven_in` are updated; there is no migration and no new ruling.
- [ ] Every harness check listed is green: rustfmt, catalog, patches, rulings, clippy, cargo tests and web tests. Report any red check by name.

**Risks.**
- **Deadlock.** The only code that takes the daily lock is the three invite write transactions. Each takes one account's lock (the caller's) before any row lock and takes no other advisory lock, so no ordering cycle forms with cancels, declines, the claim's `skip locked` or the economy lock.
- **The fake.** `prepare_between` opens its own transaction. Never call it, or `freeze_choice`, inside a transaction that is held open: in the fake that would deadlock. The steps above keep both outside.
- **Refusal order.** The early lock-free `has_room` stays in place, so a full account still gets `daily_full` before any deck error and without a game being prepared. Two round trips more per write, in Postgres only; no round-trip budget covers the daily routes (`round_trips.rs`).
- Hidden information, replay and determinism are untouched, because nothing reaches the engine.

**Open questions.**
- **Decisions made, with the alternatives rejected.**
  - An advisory lock under its own key (`jackioh.daily:`). Rejected: `select … from profiles … for update`, which serializes with every write to the profile row (R1434's username claim takes that row lock), and reusing `economy_lock_account`, which would tie daily sends to pack openings and payouts.
  - Keeping the early check. Rejected: counting only inside the write, which prepares a whole game for an account that is already full.
- **A residual, outside this issue's three counts.**
  - **The window.** When someone claims a seek, its sender's seek leaves the count when the claim commits, and the game only enters the count when it is written. The game is prepared in between, in a transaction of its own.
  - **The overrun.** A request from that sender landing in the window counts one short, so they can end at 21. `reopen_seek` writes back without a count, too.
  - **Fixing it.** The claim and the game's write would need one transaction, or the count would need to hold a claimed seek until its game is written, with `reopen_seek` retiring the old row. That reshapes the pairing.
  - **Who decides.** A person decides whether to file it as a follow-up under #3726.
````
